dedupe_keys.name: emergency response planning for chemical accident hazards key points for seveso enforcement jrc eur 27699

description: This report sets out key points and conclusions on emergency response planning for chemical accident hazards under the EU Seveso Directive (2012/18/EU), whose Article 12 makes internal emergency plans a duty of operators of upper-tier sites and external plans a duty of the authorities. It covers the challenges authorities face in checking that internal plans meet the directive and performance standards, in setting up the parallel external planning process, and in informing populations exposed to the accident scenarios of concern. It was written by Alice Doherty and Maureen Wood of the European Commission's Joint Research Centre, summarising a 2012 workshop for Seveso inspectors from EU and aligned countries organised by the Commission and the Irish Health and Safety Authority, and published on 4 April 2016 as EUR 27699 by the Publications Office of the European Union. Coverage is the EU and aligned countries. It is a free report, available online and in print, marked as a public document that can be shared. Caveats: it reflects inspectors' experience at one workshop, not a systematic survey, and the Seveso practice it describes may have changed since. For simulation it frames the scenario, warning and evacuation assumptions used in emergency response models for major chemical sites. It is related to the CSB recommendations database record in this catalogue, a US source of lessons from chemical incidents.
